subject: Portal enrollment: Tax ID clause causing registration failures
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@veridianhealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, procurement_ops@veridianhealth.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Ariba enrollment failing — Tax ID mismatch / order form acceptance

Jonas / Procurement team,

Quick heads up — we’re trying to finish vendor enrollment in Ariba so Redwood can receive POs, but the registration is failing with the attached error (see Veridian_Ariba_Error_Screenshot.png). The portal requires the Tax ID on the registration to exactly match the legal entity name on the Order Form. Our SSO/vendor data shows the supplier uses a branch Tax ID and affiliated parent company for legal contracting.

We attached the latest Order Form (OrderForm_Draft_Veridian_v2.pdf). Legal at our side flagged the MSA clause that says "Vendor Tax Identification Number must match legal entity on purchase orders" as blocking — Ariba rejects the vendor during enrollment because of the branch/parent mismatch.

Can Redwood either: 1) accept the branch Tax ID for procurement portal enrollment while keeping parent legal name on the contract, or 2) provide alternative language so the portal will accept our registration? We’re on a tight timeline — procurement needs to issue the first PO next week.

Thanks — can you advise next steps and whether legal redlines are required?

— Elena
Elena Ruiz
Senior Procurement Manager
Veridian Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: elena.ruiz@veridianhealth.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Ariba enrollment failing — Tax ID mismatch / order form acceptance

Kimberly / Marissa — forwarding Veridian’s note. Short summary: their Ariba enrollment is blocked by a Tax ID / legal-entity matching requirement. Their vendor has a branch-level Tax ID that doesn’t match the parent legal name we use on the MSA / Order Form. They need either a legal redline or an ops workaround so they can get POs next week.

Attachments: Veridian_Ariba_Error_Screenshot.png, OrderForm_Draft_Veridian_v2.pdf (from Elena).

Ask:
- Kimberly: can legal propose redline language that preserves our risk profile but allows enrollment by branch ID or evidence of parent affiliation?
- Marissa: what are our options in Ariba/Coupa for accepting a branch tax ID while keeping invoices/POs routed to the contracted legal entity? How fast can we implement a temporary manual exception?

I’m looping both so we can give Veridian a single plan today.

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: elena.ruiz@veridianhealth.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Ariba enrollment failing — Tax ID mismatch / order form acceptance

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the relevant MSA clause and the Order Form. We want to avoid a change that would expose Redwood to tax/identity misattribution risk, but we can accommodate enrollment workflows with narrowly scoped language.

Suggested redline (minimal, defensive):
"For purposes of portal enrollment and purchase order processing only, Vendor may provide a branch or subsidiary Tax Identification Number, provided Vendor also submits documentation demonstrating legal affiliation to the contracted legal entity (e.g., affiliation affidavit, subsidiary certificate, or parent company tax record). Redwood will accept such documentation for the limited purpose of enabling procurement portal enrollment and PO issuance; all contractual invoicing and liability obligations will remain with the contracted legal entity named on this Agreement."

Rationale: this lets Ariba accept their branch Tax ID during registration while keeping the contract with the legal parent. It requires evidence so we mitigate fraud/tax mismatch risk.

I attached a working PDF with the redline inserted (MSA_Redline_v3.pdf). If Ops confirms the portal can align with that approach, I’m comfortable with legal sign-off on the redline as a clean way to proceed.

KM
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal — Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: elena.ruiz@veridianhealth.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Ariba enrollment failing — Tax ID mismatch / order form acceptance

Operational perspective: we have two realistic paths — one short-term manual workaround, one longer-term portal mapping change.

Option A — Immediate workaround (recommended for PO next week):
- Veridian registers using the branch Tax ID. They upload supporting affiliation docs during registration (affidavit or certificate).
- Our Vendor Ops team performs a manual verification (1 business day) and adds a "parent legal entity" attribute to the vendor record in Ariba so that POs are issued to the contracted legal name.
- We place a note on the vendor profile and route first 2 POs for ops review (automated flag).
- Timeline: 1–2 business days after we receive docs. Low-risk and reversible.

Option B — System mapping change (preferred for scale):
- Update Ariba/Coupa field mappings to accept branch Tax IDs if the parent affiliation boolean is true. Requires config change + test.
- Timeline: ~7–10 business days (dev/config + QA).

I attached step-by-step: portal_workaround_steps.docx (includes checklist for Vendor Ops). If Kimberly’s redline is finalized, Ops can proceed with Option A right away; we’ll also kick off the config change to make this behavior standard.

Operational constraints/notes:
- We cannot alter invoicing/legal party on an executed Order Form — invoices still need to be issued by the legal entity on the contract. The workaround maps the portal registration to the contract party for PO generation only.
- If Veridian prefers to change the contracted legal entity on the Order Form, that is a separate contract amend process and will delay timeline.

If everyone agrees I’ll start the manual verification queue as soon as Elena uploads the affiliation evidence.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Vendor Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@veridianhealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Ariba enrollment failing — Tax ID mismatch / order form acceptance

Thanks, everyone — this is helpful. Veridian will proceed with Option A so we can get the first PO out next week. Action items on our side: we will pull the subsidiary affidavit and parent-company tax letter and upload to the Ariba registration portal today (ETA: EOD).

Requests:
- Kimberly: can you insert the redline language into the next Order Form/MSA iteration and confirm sign-off by EOD tomorrow so we don’t re-open negotiations?
- Marissa: please confirm you’ll start the manual verification queue once we upload the docs and advise the first PO routing/approval flow (I need the name of the Redwood contact who will approve the flagged POs).

If we can close these two items today/tomorrow Veridian will accept the temporary mapping and we’ll consider the longer-term portal config change in partnership.

Appreciate the quick coordination.

— Elena
Elena Ruiz
Senior Procurement Manager
Veridian Health
